questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to save water at home
Why date palms need so much sun
Why deserts are getting bigger
A new liquid clay technology helping farmers in a very dry place
questions.why: They visit Yuma, where liquid clay is helping farmers grow fruit and vegetables in the desert.

questions.q: How many people live in 'water stressed' countries?
options: About half of the world's population, mainly in Africa
Over two billion, around a quarter of the world
Around 70 million
About three billion
questions.why: Beth says over two billion people, around a quarter of the world's population, live in them.

questions.q: How much of the world's fresh water is used by agriculture?
options: About 25%
About 50%
About 70%
About 90% of it
questions.why: Beth says agriculture uses 'a massive 70%' of the world's fresh water.

questions.q: What is the situation for farmers in Yuma?
options: They face the worst drought in 500 years and pump water from rivers
They have plenty of rain, but the soil is too poor for most fruit trees
They have stopped growing dates
They get free water from Mexico
questions.why: Yuma is experiencing its worst drought in 500 years, forcing farmers to pump river water.

questions.q: According to reporter Anthony Wallace, why is sandy desert soil a problem?
options: Water drains through it quickly, so roots struggle to grow
It is too heavy for plants
It contains harmful chemicals from the farms that were there before
It holds too much water
questions.why: He says sandy soil has gaps so water drains quickly, making it hard for roots to establish.

questions.q: What does Ole Sivertsen claim about his liquid clay?
options: It is very cheap for all farmers
It doubles the amount of water that trees can take from the sandy soil
It halves water use, and farmers get their money back within two years
It only works on vegetables
questions.why: Neil says Ole claims it halves the water needed and most farmers make back their investment within two years.

questions.q: What is presenter Myra Anubi worried about?
options: That the liquid clay is much too expensive for most ordinary farmers to buy
That changing the soil like this could cause problems in the future
That farmers won't want to use it
That dates will taste different
questions.why: She wonders whether manipulating soil could be 'causing problems down the line'.

questions.q: How does Anthony Wallace respond to Myra's worry?
options: He says there are definitely no risks
He says the product has already been banned in several parts of the US
He agrees it should not be used
He says only time will tell, but the liquid clay uses no chemicals
questions.why: He says 'only time will tell', but Ole stressed it uses only clay, air and water.
